key_insight: ROWBench/PROWBench highlights a gap in current video-model evaluation: models can look realistic while still failing to follow fine-grained, program-specified events. The paper introduces a benchmark designed to test whether generated videos truly render what the program specifies, not just what looks plausible.
problem_solved: Current benchmarks mostly measure visual quality, controllability, or broad physical/instruction adherence, but they rarely check exact fidelity to explicit, program-defined world events and interactions. This paper addresses that missing evaluation layer for programmable world models.
method: Construct a benchmark of 170 programmatically generated episodes with explicit event rules and interactions.
Evaluate video models on their ability to faithfully render fine-grained, specified world dynamics.
Compare model outputs against program-defined ground truth to detect mismatches between visuals and executable dynamics.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more rigorous way to measure whether video and world models can serve as reliable foundations for games, simulators, and interactive environments. It helps identify models that are visually impressive but still unreliable for rule-following generation.
